entry.title: Confirm presentation and current danger
entry.scope: Entry, actual treatment exposure and current response are separate. Unknown remains unconfirmed.

fields.label: Medical / neurologic emergency now?
fields.threshold: Focal deficit, unresponsiveness, seizure/status, airway, breathing or circulatory compromise is an emergency; do not use a behavioural-sedation route first.

fields.label: Immediate harm risk?
options: Yes · violent / cannot be kept safe
fields.threshold: Separate immediate risk to the person, staff or others from a medical/neuro emergency. Use trained local safety support.

fields.label: Most likely cause
fields.threshold: Make a provisional cause from history, observations, examination, glucose, oxygenation, medicines and toxidrome. A behavioural label does not exclude medical illness.

fields.label: Verbal de-escalation / environment
fields.threshold: When feasible, use calm communication, reduced stimulation and a collaborative oral route before parenteral medication.

fields.label: Medication route if needed
fields.threshold: Offer oral medication when the person can cooperate. Parenteral treatment requires staff, monitoring and product-specific preparation.

fields.label: ED dose-reference scope
options: Monitored ED · 18–65 · not pregnant · not frail
fields.threshold: ACEP’s severe-agitation policy is ED-only and excludes pregnancy and people over 65. The source-backed dose references are withheld outside this explicit scope.

fields.label: Airway / breathing / monitoring for parenteral medicine
fields.threshold: Parenteral benzodiazepines can cause oversedation and respiratory depression, especially with CNS depressants. Resolve airway/breathing/monitoring concerns before a dose reference.

fields.label: QT / cardiovascular review for antipsychotic route
fields.threshold: NICE advises avoiding IM haloperidol plus promethazine with cardiovascular disease, prolonged QT or no ECG. Do not infer an antipsychotic route is safe.

fields.label: Parkinson disease / Lewy-body dementia
fields.threshold: Dopamine-blocking agents can be unsafe in Parkinson disease or dementia with Lewy bodies; obtain an appropriate alternative plan.

fields.label: Calming medicine already given?
options: Given · agent, dose and time recorded
fields.threshold: Reconcile the exact product, dose, route, timing, response, observations and adverse effects before any subsequent medicine.

fields.label: Current response
fields.threshold: Persistent agitation needs renewed assessment. New medical danger or adverse effect overrides an initial-regimen route.

quickReference.summary: First separate medical danger from immediate safety risk, then target the most likely cause and reassess every exposure.
recognition: Agitation can reflect medical illness, delirium, intoxication, withdrawal or psychiatric illness.
redFlags: Focal deficit, unresponsiveness, seizure/status, airway/breathing/circulatory compromise.
Worsening after a calming medicine or respiratory adverse effect.

steps.text: Use verbal de-escalation and an oral route when safely possible.

guides.title: Systemic Corticosteroids
guides.reviewLabel: Focused source review · mixed evidence strength
guides.reviewNotice: Every indication has its own entry criteria, regimen and evidence strength, from randomised trials to observational practice only. No dose carries between indications and the guide never converts between glucocorticoids.
guides.guideVersion: Focused adult review 2026-09-23
guides.resourceNotice: Internal hospital resource tables are omitted from this shared edition.
guides.scope: Adult inpatient systemic corticosteroid decisions: which indications have a source regimen, the exact regimen and entry criteria for each, pre-exposure infection screening, glucose and ulcer-risk safeguards, Pneumocystis prophylaxis, and stopping. Not a complete immunosuppression, rheumatology, transplant, oncology-supportive, meningitis or paediatric corticosteroid protocol, and not a dose converter.
reviewLimitations: NTUH public product pages were checked anonymously on 2026-11-07 for identity and label strength only. The catalog snapshot is dated 2026-08-28; these checks do not establish current stock, absence of an alternative, substitution, preparation, orderability or patient suitability.

Each indication rests on a different source of a different strength: randomised trials for septic shock, ARDS, COVID-19, severe community-acquired pneumonia and COPD duration; guideline statements for asthma, Pneumocystis and adrenal insufficiency; and observational practice only for acute ILD exacerbations and radiation pneumonitis. The guide shows which is which and does not level them.

GOLD 2026 was confirmed to recommend systemic corticosteroids for up to 5 days in moderate and severe exacerbations through the published report landing page and secondary summaries; the full 2026 report PDF was not directly read, so the exact dose sentence is carried from REDUCE, which was read as the primary trial.

The septic-shock branch follows the SSC 2026 contract already recorded in this project: a conditional suggestion for IV corticosteroids with no mandated cortisol result and no fixed vasopressor threshold. Additional vasopressor-dose/duration or cortisol-testing prerequisites from unverified protocol text are flagged for source reconciliation.

The ARDS day-14 safety signal comes from LaSRS. A 2025 observational analysis has questioned whether day 14 is a genuine boundary, so this is presented as a reason for specialist review rather than a settled prohibition.

The public Solu-Cortef injection and Florinef tablet identities do not resolve oral hydrocortisone product/strength or current availability. Confirm the actual product independently; a dated catalog cannot establish absence.
Local doses, schedules and conditions require local reconciliation; nothing here establishes current orderability.

Dose equivalence is stated once, for review, and is deliberately not applied: the guide never converts a dose between glucocorticoids or routes. The Calculator’s steroid equivalence card requires explicit manual entry for that.

entry.title: Which indication, and are its entry criteria met?
entry.guidance: Every regimen in this guide belongs to exactly one indication and appears only after that indication’s criteria are reviewed and met. Unknown is not met, and no dose is carried between indications.

source.label: SSC 2026 adult guideline — corticosteroids in septic shock

entry.scope: Indication, entry criteria, regimen, screening and stopping are separate findings. Unknown is not met.

fields.label: Review timing
fields.threshold: Starting, continuing and stopping are different decisions; they do not share the same safeguards.

fields.label: Indication group?
fields.threshold: Each group has its own entry criteria and its own reviewed regimen. No dose carries between groups.

fields.label: Which lung inflammation?
options: Acute exacerbation of interstitial lung disease

fields.label: Adrenal presentation?
fields.threshold: Crisis is a clinical emergency diagnosis; do not wait for a cortisol result in a shocked patient.

fields.label: Primary or secondary?
fields.threshold: Mineralocorticoid replacement applies to primary adrenal insufficiency only.

fields.label: Entry criteria for this indication?
fields.threshold: Unknown is not “met”. The exact criteria for the selected indication are listed in the first stage.

fields.label: Pre-exposure infection screen?
options: Reviewed · no untreated TB, fungal or Strongyloides risk
fields.threshold: Active tuberculosis, untreated invasive fungal infection and Strongyloides exposure are the screening triggers.

fields.label: Influenza suspected or confirmed?
fields.threshold: Influenza changes the pneumonia branches; it does not remove a COPD or asthma exacerbation indication.

fields.label: Gastroduodenal ulcer or bleeding risk?
options: NSAID, anticoagulant, prior ulcer, or ICU stress-ulcer criteria
fields.threshold: Acid suppression follows these risk factors; a corticosteroid alone is not an automatic indication.

fields.label: Expected ≥20 mg prednisolone-equivalent daily for ≥4 weeks?
fields.threshold: This is the Pneumocystis-prophylaxis and adrenal-suppression trigger, not a dose recommendation.

stages.empty: Select the indication and review its criteria.

quickReference.summary: Name the indication, check that indication’s entry criteria, then use only that indication’s regimen — and decide screening, glucose monitoring, ulcer risk, Pneumocystis prophylaxis and the stop date at the same time.
recognition: Indications with a randomised-trial regimen: septic shock, moderate-to-severe ARDS, COVID-19 needing oxygen, severe community-acquired pneumonia, COPD exacerbation duration.
Indications with guideline regimens: asthma exacerbation, Pneumocystis pneumonia, adrenal insufficiency, tumour-related raised intracranial pressure.
Indications resting on observational practice only: acute exacerbation of ILD, radiation pneumonitis.
redFlags: Suspected adrenal crisis — give hydrocortisone 100 mg IV or IM immediately; do not wait for a cortisol result in a shocked patient.
Active tuberculosis, untreated invasive fungal infection, or Strongyloides exposure risk before immunosuppression.
Suspected primary CNS lymphoma before biopsy — corticosteroid can make the histology non-diagnostic.
Starting a corticosteroid in persistent ARDS at or after day 14, or in influenza pneumonia, without specialist review.

steps.text: Choose one indication and review its explicit entry criteria. Unknown is not met, and no regimen appears until they are.
Use only the regimen recorded for that indication. Do not carry a dose across indications or convert between glucocorticoids from memory.

Tuberculosis, invasive fungal infection and Strongyloides before exposure; glucose monitoring, ulcer-risk-driven acid suppression, and Pneumocystis prophylaxis at ≥20 mg prednisolone-equivalent for ≥4 weeks.
Short defined courses stop without a taper; prolonged or repeated courses taper, and replacement therapy is reduced to maintenance rather than stopped.
Re-check the indication, response and stop date. Improvement on a steroid is not confirmation of the diagnosis.

monitoring: Capillary glucose through the course, weighted to afternoon and evening values when the steroid is dosed in the morning.
Infection signs, blood pressure, mood, sleep and — for longer courses — bone protection, muscle weakness and adrenal suppression.
The recorded stop or taper date at each review, including what appears on the discharge medication list.

guides.scope: Adult anticoagulant-related bleeding triage, agent-specific initial-regimen review, response/rebleed review and individualized restart-decision review. It is not an order set, stock check, transfusion protocol, procedure plan, automatic restart protocol or authorization.
reviewLimitations: NTUH public product pages were checked anonymously on 2026-11-07 for identity and label strength only. The catalog snapshot is dated 2026-08-28; these checks do not establish current stock, absence of an alternative, substitution, preparation, orderability or patient suitability.

ACC 2020 is the broad oral-anticoagulant pathway source. FDA’s December 2025 safety/availability communication means its historical andexanet regimen is not emitted; Taiwan/NTUH availability and governance were not verified.

Acute GI bleeding is deliberately routed to ACG/CAG 2022 qualifications, which conditionally advise against several routine reversal approaches. Intracranial haemorrhage is routed to the AHA/ASA 2022 emergency pathway; spinal and other neurocritical bleeding require their own urgent route.

NTUH public formulary codes are references only: BER1EB25 (Beriplex four-factor PCC), KAT1EB04 (phytonadione), PRA1QB42 (idarucizumab) and PRF1QB08 (protamine). They do not establish current stock, restriction, orderability or patient suitability.

No automatic anticoagulant restart, bridging strategy, transfusion plan, antiplatelet reversal, trauma/massive-haemorrhage, pregnancy, cardiac-surgery, HIT, fondaparinux or procedure-specific protocol is implemented.

fields.label: Review point?
fields.threshold: Initial treatment, response/rebleeding, and any later anticoagulant decision are separate reviews.

fields.label: Immediate bleeding emergency?
fields.threshold: ABC compromise, shock, ongoing major blood loss, impaired consciousness, focal neurology or airway risk requires urgent action now.

fields.label: Bleeding severity?
fields.threshold: ACC major bleed: critical site, haemodynamic instability, haemoglobin fall ≥2 g/dL, or ≥2 RBC units.

fields.label: Bleed setting / site?
options: Spinal or other intracranial / neurocritical bleed
Other critical site / uncontrolled major bleed
Major by physiology / blood loss; no critical site identified
fields.threshold: Acute GI bleeding and intracranial haemorrhage have source-specific qualifications; do not silently apply a generic card.

fields.label: Exact anticoagulant?
fields.threshold: Do not select a reversal strategy from an incomplete medication list or a drug class alone.

fields.label: Likely clinically relevant residual effect?
fields.threshold: Base this on exact agent, dose, last administration, renal/liver context and any appropriate assay; a normal PT/INR does not exclude a factor-Xa inhibitor effect.

fields.label: Agent, dose, last time and clearance context reconciled?
fields.threshold: For heparins, record units or mg and elapsed time. For DOACs, document the exact drug and renal context.

fields.label: Resuscitation and source-control status?
fields.threshold: Reversal must not delay airway/circulation support, endoscopic, procedural, surgical or other definitive haemostasis.

fields.label: Has an initial reversal / haemostatic action already been given?
options: Given — record exact agent, amount and time
fields.threshold: This prevents a prior dose being presented again as a new initial regimen.

fields.label: Selected agent’s current local product and safety gate?
options: Confirmed appropriate in the local emergency plan
fields.threshold: Before confirming: PCC—review HIT/heparin allergy, DIC and thrombosis risk; protamine—prior reaction/risk and resuscitation readiness; idarucizumab—hypersensitivity. Also verify current local product, restriction and protocol.

fields.label: Pre-treatment INR band?
fields.threshold: Use the pretreatment INR. Spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage has a separate AHA lower-INR consideration.

fields.label: Time since the enoxaparin dose?
fields.threshold: Protamine only partially reverses enoxaparin. The exact enoxaparin dose must also be known.

fields.label: Course after the first action?
fields.threshold: Current deterioration overrides an earlier improvement or completed initial regimen.

fields.label: Restart decision review complete?
options: Indication, thrombotic risk, rebleed risk and patient goals reviewed
fields.threshold: This records a review only. It does not select an anticoagulant, dose, bridge or restart time.

quickReference.summary: Stabilize, classify severity/site and exact exposure, control the source, then review any reversal and later restart decision separately.
recognition: Major bleeding: critical site, haemodynamic instability, haemoglobin fall ≥2 g/dL, or ≥2 RBC units.
Exact agent, dose, last time and clearance context determine whether a residual effect is plausible.
redFlags: Airway/ABC compromise, shock, ongoing major blood loss, impaired consciousness or focal neurology.
Intracranial haemorrhage, spinal/neurocritical bleeding and acute GI bleeding require source-specific routes; do not use a generic card without the setting.

steps.text: Support ABCs and control the bleeding source in parallel.
Confirm exact anticoagulant, dose, last time, clearance and whether any reversal was already given.
Ongoing bleeding/rebleed needs a new specialist review; a later restart decision is individualized.

monitoring: Reassess haemodynamics, bleeding, haemoglobin/testing and source-control findings at a defined review point.
Monitor for thrombosis after reversal; do not infer a restart agent, dose or time from this guide.

reviewLimitations: The BSH guideline is the branch source for recognition, initial response, mild/severe distinctions and symptom-directed investigation. It explicitly does not provide detailed cardiac/respiratory-failure or bacterial-sepsis treatment protocols.

No local blood-bank SOP, component identity, compatibility/crossmatch order, product availability, administration preparation, or restart authority was verified here. Those remain local transfusion-service decisions.

entry.title: Confirm presentation and immediate danger
entry.scope: Unknown findings remain unconfirmed; initial treatment and response are separate.

fields.label: Review point
fields.essential: Initial safety and later response are separate; an unknown phase never hides a suspected reaction.

fields.label: New symptom or sign plausibly related to a recent component?
fields.essential: A suspected reaction triggers the stop-and-assess response before a subtype is assigned.

fields.label: Implicated component status
fields.essential: Stop a suspected component and keep compatible-saline access; completed units are not restarted here.

fields.label: Immediate identity, component and observation check
fields.essential: Check identity/label and component, assess ABC/observations, and notify the transfusion service.

fields.label: Current airway, breathing or circulation compromise?
fields.essential: Current ABC compromise overrides every earlier label: call emergency support and do not restart.

fields.label: Current symptom pattern after immediate safety review
options: Suspected anaphylaxis · airway, breathing or circulation involvement
Sustained fever/rigors, shock, pain, dark urine, or bleeding
Acute dyspnoea / hypoxaemia; allergy not the explanation
Alternative explanation more likely after assessment
fields.essential: This is a working pattern; severe reactions can overlap and treatment does not wait for tests.

fields.label: Strictly isolated mild pattern?
options: Yes — fever 38–<39 C / rise 1–<2 C, or rash only
fields.essential: Mild means isolated fever/rash with no concerning feature or observation change.

fields.label: Hemolysis or bacterial-contamination concern?
options: Not supported after clinical and laboratory review
fields.essential: Sustained fever/rigors, shock, pain, dark urine or bleeding need haemolysis/bacterial review.

fields.label: Pulmonary assessment beyond timing
options: Pulmonary transfusion reaction not supported after assessment
fields.essential: Time alone never establishes TRALI or TACO; reconcile oxygenation, imaging and overload evidence.

fields.label: Current course after the first response
fields.essential: Repeat ABC and observations; improvement does not replace work-up or authorize a restart.

fields.label: If resumption is contemplated, is explicit local clearance documented?
options: Yes — accountable clearance and direct observation
No — clearance absent / serious cause open
fields.essential: Only explicit local clearance plus direct observation can support a contemplated resumption.

stages.title: Recognize and stop the implicated component
stages.empty: Establish whether there is a suspected acute reaction before assigning a benign explanation.

stages.title: Immediate safety and severity
stages.empty: Current ABC findings and the first-response checks remain separate from later classification.

stages.title: Pattern-directed work-up and treatment
stages.empty: Use the symptom pattern and investigations; timing alone does not diagnose a pulmonary reaction.

stages.title: Reassess before any future component decision
stages.empty: Improvement does not itself authorize resumption of an implicated transfusion.

quickReference.summary: Stop the component, assess ABC and identity, then use the evolving symptom pattern rather than a premature subtype label.
recognition: New fever, rigors, rash, pain, dark urine, dyspnoea, hypoxaemia, hypotension, bleeding, or anxiety during or after a component can be an acute reaction.
redFlags: Any airway, breathing or circulation compromise; severe dyspnoea/hypoxaemia; shock; new bleeding; dark urine/loin pain; sustained fever or rigors.
Suspected anaphylaxis, haemolysis, bacterial contamination, TRALI, TACO, or mixed pulmonary reaction: do not restart the implicated component.

steps.text: Stop the implicated component, maintain IV access with saline, check identity/label and inspect the component.
Treat current ABC compromise immediately; investigations must not delay severe-reaction care.
Use explicit local transfusion-service/clinical clearance and direct observation for any contemplated resumption.

monitoring: Repeat ABC and observations while symptoms evolve; reassess new fever, respiratory findings, pain, urine change, bleeding and haemodynamics.
Communicate urgency and clinical pattern to the transfusion service; retain implicated material through the local process.

guides.scope: Adult inpatient HF review: emergency routing, congestion/perfusion, source-labelled loop references, cautious nitrate consideration, and a handoff to GDMT and discharge review. It uses AHA/ACC 2022 and ACC 2024 sources; ESC 2026 review is pending. It is not a diagnosis engine, medication order interface, dose calculator, or discharge authority.
reviewLimitations: The current 2026 ESC material defines HFrEF as LVEF <50%, while the 2022 US guideline used here uses ≤40%. A dedicated ESC 2026 source mode remains review pending; this engine does not claim ESC 2026 implementation.
Detailed loop-diuretic dosing, four-pillar GDMT titration and discharge planning are outside this guide.
Orderability, formulation and local protocol remain separate reviews.

entry.title: Confirm HF presentation and current stability
entry.guidance: Emergency physiology overrides phase. Acute decongestion and chronic optimization use separate current findings; unknown never means safe or absent.
entry.scope: Entry, current danger and treatment response are separate findings. Unknown remains unconfirmed.

fields.label: Review lane
fields.essential: Emergency findings override the lane.

fields.label: Emergency finding now?
options: Present — shock, severe respiratory failure, ischemia, unstable rhythm, or mechanical concern
No immediate emergency finding after assessment
fields.threshold: Assess ABCs, perfusion, escalating support, ischemia, rhythm and mechanical concern.

fields.label: HF working route?
fields.threshold: This is a working route, not a diagnosis; reconcile current evidence and alternatives.

fields.label: Congestion now?
fields.threshold: Use symptoms, examination, weight/fluids and objective data in context.

fields.label: Perfusion now?
fields.threshold: Use BP with mentation, extremities, urine output, lactate and organ trajectory.

fields.label: Trigger review?
options: Identified and being managed in parallel
fields.threshold: Review ischemia, rhythm, BP, infection, medicines, renal change, PE and mechanical causes.

fields.label: Loop exposure?
options: Home drug, daily dose, route and last dose/time reconciled
Recent IV total dose, time and response window reconciled
fields.threshold: Never infer loop-naive status; reconcile agent, total dose, route, time, delivery and response.

fields.label: Loop safety?
fields.threshold: Review perfusion/BP, renal/electrolytes, dialysis, allergy, exposure/delivery and local protocol.

fields.label: Response to recent IV loop?
fields.threshold: Before another action, record symptoms, support, output, balance, weight, perfusion and renal/electrolytes.

fields.label: Hypertensive pulmonary-edema pattern?
options: Yes — reviewed hypertensive pulmonary-edema / afterload pattern
No — this pattern is not established
fields.threshold: Nitrates are not routine; review pattern, BP, perfusion and cause first.

fields.label: Nitrate safety?
options: No systemic hypotension or other entered contraindication after review
Hypotension / contraindication concern or review incomplete
fields.threshold: Confirm pressure/perfusion, contraindications, interactions and monitored local setup.

fields.label: Phenotype for legacy GDMT?
options: HFrEF explicitly confirmed by the treating team
Other phenotype or phenotype remains uncertain
fields.threshold: Use the documented phenotype and LVEF source/date; no cut-off is computed here.

fields.label: Stable GDMT window?
options: Active decompensation, hypotension/hypoperfusion, or other blocker remains
fields.threshold: A GDMT readiness review checks the four pillars, exact drug/formulation, safety, tolerance and ownership.

fields.label: Transition plan?
options: Plan reconciled; remaining items have a named owner and review date
Residual congestion or unresolved transition gap
fields.threshold: Review congestion, oral plan, medicines, labs, education/access and named early follow-up.

stages.empty: Complete the current assessment.

stages.title: Emergency / low-perfusion escalation
stages.empty: Escalate urgent physiology before routine therapy.

stages.title: Congestion, exposure & response

quickReference.summary: Treat emergency physiology first. Review congestion and perfusion together, then reconcile actual loop exposure and response before a repeat or chronic-GDMT decision.
recognition: State the current review lane; acute treatment response and chronic optimization are separate states.
Confirm current congestion and perfusion; a prior HF label or stale medication list is not enough.
redFlags: Shock/hypoperfusion, altered mentation, severe respiratory failure or escalating support.
Ongoing ischemia, unstable arrhythmia, syncope, or acute valvular/mechanical concern.
Worsening after a recent loop, resistant congestion, or new renal/electrolyte concern.

steps.text: Escalate immediately; routine loop, nitrate, GDMT and discharge branches are withheld.
Require confirmed congestion, adequate perfusion, reconciled exposure and a safety review before a local loop plan.
Record symptoms, oxygen/support, urine output, balance, weight, BP/perfusion and renal/electrolytes before any repeat or intensification.
Start four-pillar GDMT review only after a compensated window is explicit.

monitoring: Trend current congestion, oxygen/support, BP/perfusion, urine output, balance, weight and kidney/electrolyte trajectory at a frequency matched to severity.
At transition, keep the oral plan, medication reconciliation, laboratory plan, education/access barriers and named early follow-up visible.

guides.title: Severely Elevated Blood Pressure
guides.reviewNotice: Acute organ injury determines the emergency route.
guides.guideVersion: Focused adult source review 2026-09-19
guides.resourceNotice: Internal hospital resource tables are omitted from this shared edition.
guides.scope: Adult acute-care severe BP entry: accurate repeat measurement, new/worsening target-organ-damage distinction, independent urgent signals, condition-specific exception routing, and separated initial-versus-response review.
reviewLimitations: NTUH public product pages were checked anonymously on 2026-11-07 for identity and label strength only. The catalog snapshot is dated 2026-08-28; these checks do not establish current stock, absence of an alternative, substitution, preparation, orderability or patient suitability.
This is not a BP calculator, diagnosis, patient chart, medication-administration record, prescription, order set, infusion protocol, target authorization, or discharge decision.

All findings default to unknown. The guide never treats a missing repeat BP, missing acute-organ assessment, unentered emergency priority, unclassified exception, unverified prior treatment or absent response as a negative finding.

Aortic disease, acute stroke/ICH, pregnancy/postpartum severe hypertension, acute coronary syndrome and pulmonary oedema require condition-specific evaluation and targets. The general nonstroke/nonpregnant target is deliberately withheld until no compelling exception is identified.

Only the eligible general emergency route can show the source Table 26 nicardipine or labetalol regimen after immediate emergency priority is explicitly absent and its strategy, safety and prior-exposure gates are complete. No preparation, line, combination, exception-route regimen, orderability or administration record is generated.
Exact product identity, current availability, regimen alignment, patient suitability and authorization remain separate checks.

entry.title: Confirm BP and acute organ injury
entry.scope: Entry, current danger and treatment response are separate findings. Unknown remains unconfirmed.

fields.label: Review point?
options: After an initial BP action · review response
fields.threshold: Initial action and response are separate. Unknown does not restart treatment.

fields.label: Accurate repeat BP?
options: Repeat remains in the severe range
Repeat is below the severe range
fields.threshold: Repeat with correct cuff and position. ACC/AHA 2025: >180 systolic and/or >120 diastolic; the number alone does not establish emergency.
fields.help: Record measured systolic/diastolic values and time separately. Pain, distress, acute illness and measurement technique can alter the reading.

fields.label: New or worsening acute target-organ damage?
fields.threshold: Assess new/worsening brain, heart/lung, aortic, kidney or retinal/microvascular injury. Chronic findings alone do not establish emergency.
fields.help: Examples include hypertensive encephalopathy, intracranial haemorrhage or acute ischaemic stroke, acute coronary syndrome, acute pulmonary oedema/heart failure, acute aortic syndrome, acute kidney injury, retinal haemorrhage/papilloedema or microangiopathy. Pregnancy-related severe hypertension needs its own route.

fields.label: Immediate emergency priority?
fields.threshold: Independent of phase: ABC compromise, neurologic change, seizure, chest/back pain, collapse or rapid deterioration needs urgent action now.

fields.label: Specific emergency pattern?
options: No specific pattern identified after assessment
Acute ischaemic stroke or intracranial haemorrhage
Pregnancy / postpartum severe hypertension or eclampsia concern
Acute coronary syndrome or pulmonary oedema / acute heart failure
Other acute target-organ damage · no compelling exception identified
fields.threshold: Aortic, stroke/ICH, pregnancy and acute cardiac/pulmonary patterns use condition-specific targets, not the general percentage target.

fields.label: Selected eligible initial strategy?
fields.threshold: Shown only for the eligible nonstroke, nonpregnant general-emergency route. Named exceptions use their own pathway.

fields.label: Nicardipine safety gate?
fields.threshold: ACC/AHA 2025 Table 26 lists advanced aortic stenosis as a contraindication.

fields.label: Labetalol safety gate?
fields.threshold: Do not use with reactive airway/obstructive lung disease; avoid with bradycardia, 2nd/3rd-degree block or decompensated HF.

fields.label: Prior BP-agent exposure?
fields.threshold: Before an initial regimen or response decision, reconcile agent, route, timing and total exposure. Never repeat a loading/initial sequence automatically.

fields.label: Current BP / organ-damage response?
options: Improving / stable within a named plan
Persistent or worsening BP / organ findings
Excessive fall or new hypoperfusion concern
fields.threshold: A lower BP alone does not establish recovery. Reassess the organ finding and harm from excessive reduction alongside the measured BP trend.

stages.title: Confirm BP and acute organ status
stages.empty: Confirm a credible repeat BP and whether new or worsening acute target-organ damage is present.

stages.title: Immediate safety and exception route
stages.empty: Keep immediate emergency features and named condition-specific exceptions visible.

stages.title: Choose the bounded BP route
stages.empty: Classify the acute target-organ context before considering a general BP-reduction target.

stages.title: Keep initial action and response separate
stages.empty: Record whether this is initial planning or a response review, then reconcile actual exposure and current organ status.

quickReference.summary: Repeat BP accurately, separate acute target-organ damage from the number, preserve emergency exceptions, and keep initial action distinct from response.
recognition: AHA 2024 distinguishes hypertensive emergency from asymptomatic markedly elevated inpatient BP by new or worsening acute target-organ damage, not BP alone.
Confirm a credible repeat BP and screen current neurologic, cardiac/pulmonary, aortic, kidney and microvascular findings. Unknown does not establish absence.
Immediate emergency priority is independent of phase; aortic, stroke/ICH, pregnancy and acute cardiopulmonary patterns need condition-specific targets.
redFlags: Airway/breathing compromise, altered consciousness, seizure, active focal deficit, collapse, rapidly worsening course or acute chest/back symptoms.
Suspected acute aortic syndrome, acute stroke/ICH, pregnancy/postpartum severe hypertension/eclampsia concern, acute coronary syndrome or pulmonary oedema.
Excessive BP fall, new hypoperfusion, persistent/worsening organ findings, unknown treatment exposure or a contradiction between a named emergency pattern and an “absent” organ-damage entry.

steps.text: Repeat BP with credible technique and assess new or worsening acute target-organ damage before classifying the route.
Aortic disease, stroke/ICH, pregnancy and acute cardiopulmonary patterns bypass the general percentage target and use their own urgent pathway.

Only for a confirmed nonstroke, nonpregnant emergency without a compelling exception: ACC/AHA 2025 limits first-hour SBP reduction to no more than 25%, then if stable toward <160/100 mmHg over 2–6 hours in monitored care.
Without acute target-organ damage, do not reflexively lower BP with IV treatment; review measurement, reversible causes, home regimen and follow-up through the treating team.
After any initial action, reconcile actual exposure and the named condition-specific target before judging response or adding treatment.

monitoring: For hypertensive emergency, ACC/AHA 2025 recommends ICU admission for continuous BP and target-organ monitoring with consideration of appropriate parenteral therapy.
Trend BP with timing, current organ findings, perfusion and actual treatment exposure. A lower BP alone does not establish recovery.
Use urgent condition-specific reassessment for worsening findings or excessive BP reduction; this guide does not select a repeat or second-agent regimen.

guides.title: Syncope
guides.reviewNotice: Focused adult event, risk and reassessment review.
guides.guideVersion: Focused adult source review 2026-09-19
guides.resourceNotice: Internal hospital resource tables are omitted from this shared edition.
guides.scope: Adult event recognition, initial risk assessment, directed testing and reassessment. Not a complete specialist syncope or automatic discharge protocol.
reviewLimitations: ESC 2018 official recommendation slides reviewed; ACC/AHA/HRS 2017 official summary used for routine-test cautions. No newer replacement found on the inspected society hubs.
No automatic risk-score calculation, device therapy or empirical syncope medication regimen.

sources.label: ESC 2018 Syncope — official guideline teaching slides
ACC/AHA/HRS 2017 Syncope — recommendations summary

entry.title: Was this syncope, and is there current danger?
entry.scope: Entry, current danger and treatment response are separate findings. Unknown remains unconfirmed.

fields.label: Was the event consistent with syncope?
options: Brief loss of consciousness; rapid, complete recovery
fields.threshold: Confirm rapid onset, short duration and spontaneous complete recovery. Ask witnesses; a fall or dizziness alone is not syncope.

fields.label: Current emergency features?
fields.threshold: Persistent altered consciousness, shock, ongoing chest pain/dyspnea, focal deficit, major bleeding or serious injury requires urgent assessment.

fields.label: History and examination complete?
fields.threshold: Review trigger, posture, prodrome, witness account, medications, cardiac/family history, injury and examination.

fields.label: Reviewed 12-lead ECG?
fields.threshold: Review ischemia, conduction block, bradycardia, ventricular arrhythmia, QT, Brugada pattern, pre-excitation and device function.

fields.label: Other high-risk features?
fields.threshold: Exertional/supine event, preceding palpitations, severe heart disease, unexplained SBP <90, bleeding or unexplained murmur. Review short/no prodrome and family sudden death in context.

fields.label: Supine and standing BP/HR review?
fields.threshold: When safe, measure supine and during 3 minutes standing. A fall ≥20 systolic or ≥10 diastolic, or SBP <90, with reproduced symptoms supports orthostatic syncope.

fields.label: Mechanism supported by the assessment?
fields.threshold: A typical trigger and prodrome support reflex syncope. Do not infer a benign cause from a negative test alone.

fields.label: Additional testing indication?
fields.threshold: Choose tests for the suspected cause. There is no routine syncope panel.

fields.label: Current course after evaluation / treatment?
options: Recovered; no recurrence or ongoing symptoms
fields.threshold: An earlier recovery or benign label cannot override the current course.

fields.label: Follow-up and safety plan established?
fields.threshold: Document reassessment, return precautions, injury risk and locally applicable driving/work advice. This is not an automatic discharge decision.

quickReference.summary: Confirm the event, assess danger and choose cause-directed evaluation.
recognition: Brief loss of consciousness with rapid onset and spontaneous complete recovery.
redFlags: Current instability, persistent altered consciousness, focal deficit, major bleeding or serious injury.
Exertional/supine events, concerning ECG or structural cardiac disease warrant prompt risk review.

steps.text: History, examination, ECG and safe orthostatic BP/HR; targeted tests only.
High risk needs prompt monitored evaluation. Unknown findings or recurrent symptoms do not establish low risk.

monitoring: Repeat current safety, symptoms and ECG as indicated; document rationale for disposition.

guides.reviewNotice: Early assessment and escalation; specialist antithrombotic and reperfusion prescriptions are outside this guide.
guides.guideVersion: 2025 ACS guideline + 2021 chest pain guideline
guides.resourceNotice: Internal hospital resource tables are omitted from this shared edition.
guides.scope: Adult early chest-pain / possible ACS assessment, selected initial therapy and reassessment; not a full specialist ACS protocol.
reviewLimitations: Source review covers early recognition, escalation, aspirin, selective oxygen/nitrates and reassessment. It does not cover the full 2025 ACS guideline.

Local regimens, product availability and orderability are separate from source-based recommendations. Some marketed sublingual nitroglycerin strengths (for example 0.6 mg) differ from the guideline 0.3/0.4 mg regimen.

sources.label: 2025 ACC/AHA ACS guideline — early assessment and treatment
Nitrostat product label — sGC contraindication
2025 guideline full text — ACC Georgia chapter copy inspected
2021 AHA/ACC Chest Pain guideline — official slide set

entry.title: Confirm presentation and urgency
entry.guidance: Assess ECG, stability and dangerous alternatives first. A nondiagnostic ECG or improved pain does not exclude ACS.

source.label: 2025 ACC/AHA ACS guideline — early assessment and treatment

entry.scope: Unknown findings remain unconfirmed; assess immediate danger before selecting a treatment phase.

fields.label: Clinical assessment of ACS likelihood?
fields.threshold: Pain relief or one normal ECG does not exclude ACS. Consider anginal equivalents and dangerous mimics.

fields.label: Current ECG assessment?
fields.threshold: Acquire and review a 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes. Repeat with persistent/recurrent symptoms; obtain posterior/right-sided leads when indicated.

fields.label: Current clinical stability?
fields.threshold: Hypotension, poor perfusion, malignant arrhythmia or acute heart failure require emergency assessment. A reassuring symptom response does not override instability.

fields.label: Time-critical alternative diagnosis suspected?
fields.threshold: Consider aortic dissection, pulmonary embolism, tension pneumothorax and esophageal rupture. Resolve suspected dissection before routine antithrombotic treatment.

fields.label: Current SpO₂?
fields.threshold: Record oxygen device/context. An adequate saturation on oxygen does not establish that oxygen can be stopped.

fields.label: Aspirin contraindication review?
fields.threshold: Confirm active bleeding, true hypersensitivity, swallowing/route suitability and the differential diagnosis.

fields.label: Aspirin loading dose in this episode?
fields.threshold: Reconcile dose and time. Maintenance aspirin use is not the same as an acute loading dose.

fields.label: Current ischemic symptoms?
fields.threshold: Persistent symptoms despite initial therapy require urgent reassessment, not simply repeated symptom medication.

fields.label: Nitrate already given in this episode?
options: One or more doses already given
fields.threshold: Reconcile all doses, routes and administration times before any additional nitrate. This guide never restarts a three-dose series after treatment.

fields.label: Nitrate safety check?
fields.threshold: Check BP before each dose: avoid SBP <90 mmHg or >30 mmHg fall from baseline, suspected RV infarct, severe aortic stenosis, sGC stimulator use (e.g. riociguat), or recent PDE5 inhibitor (avanafil <12 h; sildenafil/vardenafil <24 h; tadalafil <48 h).

fields.label: Since initial assessment / treatment?
fields.threshold: Update the current ECG, stability and oxygenation above; improvement alone does not rule out ACS.

fields.label: Serial troponin / clinical pathway result?
fields.threshold: Use the local assay-specific pathway and symptom timing. Troponin injury alone does not establish type 1 MI; a low-risk conclusion also requires ECG and clinical assessment.

stages.title: Entry & urgent route
stages.empty: Complete current assessment.

stages.title: Selected early treatment
stages.empty: Establish the clinical route before medication review.

stages.title: Serial review & disposition
stages.empty: Select reassessment after initial evaluation.

quickReference.summary: Early adult ACS review with explicit emergency, contraindication and serial-assessment branches.
recognition: ECG within 10 minutes; assess perfusion and dangerous alternative diagnoses.
Use serial hs-troponin with the local assay-specific pathway.
redFlags: STEMI/equivalent, shock, electrical instability, acute heart failure or refractory ischemia.
Suspected dissection or other time-critical chest-pain mimic.

steps.text: STEMI: activate reperfusion without waiting for troponin.
Check aspirin loading already given and contraindications. Oxygen for SpO₂ <90%; nitrates require stable BP and a clear contraindication review.
Update symptoms, ECG and serial biomarkers; improvement alone is not rule-out.

monitoring: Document repeated ECG, BP, rhythm, SpO₂ and troponin timing.
Reconcile local products and all antithrombotic exposure.

guides.title: Atrial Fibrillation with RVR
guides.reviewNotice: AF recognition, acute rate control and cardioversion safeguards. Source thresholds are explicitly distinguished.
guides.guideVersion: 2023 ACC/AHA AF + 2024 ESC AF + 2025 AHA ALS
guides.resourceNotice: Internal hospital resource tables are omitted from this shared edition.
guides.scope: Adult acute AF with rapid ventricular response: entry confirmation, instability/pre-excitation escalation, a single monitored rate-control route, reassessment, and planned-cardioversion thromboembolism safeguards.
reviewLimitations: This is an adult acute-care review aid, not a diagnosis, ECG interpretation service, cardioversion procedure, defibrillator configuration, sedation plan, local medication order, anticoagulation prescription, infusion-pump protocol, medication-administration record or authorization.

AHA ACLS emergency escalation, ACC acute-rate doses and ESC/ACC cardioversion safeguards have different scopes. The 24-hour ESC and 48-hour ACC cardioversion thresholds are displayed as a source difference, not merged into a new rule.

Product selection, prepared concentration, pump/device, IV access, dose calculation, renal/hepatic adjustment, interaction review, live availability/orderability and patient-specific suitability require separate verification.

Pre-excited/wide-irregular AF, attributable instability, shock, acute heart failure, ongoing ischaemia or worsening physiology require emergency/critical-care rhythm management outside this compact engine.

sources.label: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS atrial fibrillation guideline
2024 ESC/EACTS atrial fibrillation guideline
2025 AHA Adult Tachyarrhythmia With a Pulse Algorithm

entry.title: Confirm presentation and urgency
entry.guidance: Confirm AF, exclude pre-excitation, establish a clinically rapid ventricular response and assess whether instability is attributable to the tachyarrhythmia. Urgent findings override phase selection.
entry.scope: Unknown findings remain unconfirmed; assess immediate danger before selecting a treatment phase.

fields.label: Review phase
fields.essential: Select the treatment phase. Urgent escalation remains available before selection.

fields.label: AF confirmed on a reviewed ECG?
options: No — AF not confirmed / another rhythm possible
fields.threshold: Confirm AF on the ECG; a monitor rate alone does not establish the rhythm.

fields.label: Wide-irregular rhythm or pre-excitation concern?
options: Yes — wide-irregular rhythm or pre-excitation concern
fields.threshold: Wide-irregular / pre-excited AF requires urgent review. Withhold AV-nodal blockers until excluded.

fields.label: Current ventricular response needs acute control?
options: No — no acute rapid-response route selected
fields.threshold: Assess symptoms and perfusion, not rate alone. A slower rate does not exclude an emergency.

fields.label: Instability attributable to the tachyarrhythmia?
fields.threshold: Assess hypotension, shock, altered mental status, ischemic discomfort or acute heart failure. Treat instability immediately.

fields.label: Acute trigger review
options: Trigger identified and being managed in parallel
fields.threshold: ESC advises evaluating and managing acute triggers before or in parallel with rate/rhythm control, including sepsis, fluid overload, cardiogenic shock, hypoxaemia, ischaemia, electrolytes and medication effects.

fields.label: LV function / heart-failure context
options: LVEF >40% and no decompensated heart failure
Critical illness or decompensated heart failure
fields.threshold: Diltiazem/verapamil requires an explicit LVEF >40% route. IV nondihydropyridine calcium-channel blockers should not be used with known moderate/severe LV systolic dysfunction; IV beta-blockers should not be used in decompensated heart failure.

fields.label: Current control decision
fields.threshold: Rate control, rhythm control and stroke prevention are separate decisions. Emergency cardioversion for attributable instability is not delayed for this elective/planned strategy field.

fields.label: Selected initial rate-control agent
fields.threshold: Choose one monitored rate-control strategy. Do not stack beta-blocker and diltiazem/verapamil empirically; reconcile timing, response and haemodynamics before adding another AV-nodal agent.

fields.label: Beta-blocker suitability
options: No active severe bronchospasm, important AV block, or other beta-blocker contraindication identified
Active severe bronchospasm / contraindication or concern
fields.threshold: This screen does not replace a medication, AV-conduction, perfusion or drug-interaction review. In decompensated heart failure, do not use IV beta-blocker for the routine rate-control branch.

fields.label: Recent AV-nodal therapy reconciled?
options: One recent agent given; response/timing still active
Multiple agents or timing overlap / uncertainty
fields.threshold: Before a new dose, reconcile the exact agent, dose, route, time, blood pressure/perfusion and response. Multiple AV-nodal agents can produce delayed hypotension, bradycardia or AV block.

fields.label: Observed response after the initial intervention
options: Rate, symptoms and perfusion improved adequately
Persistent rapid ventricular response despite initial strategy
fields.threshold: Reassess rhythm, rate, blood pressure, perfusion, symptoms, acute trigger and total recent AV-nodal exposure before any repeat or additional agent. A lower rate does not close the trigger or stroke-prevention review.

fields.label: First-line beta-blocker/diltiazem status after reassessment
options: Ineffective or contraindicated — documented after reassessment
fields.threshold: Digoxin is a considered fallback only when beta-blockers and nondihydropyridine calcium-channel blockers are ineffective or contraindicated. IV amiodarone is a narrower critically-ill/decompensated-HF option and may cardiovert.

fields.label: Digoxin loading eligibility reviewed?
options: Prior digoxin exposure, kidney function, potassium/magnesium, interactions and current conduction/rhythm reviewed
High risk, prior exposure, renal/electrolyte/interaction concern, or review incomplete
fields.threshold: Do not use a generic digoxin loading regimen until prior exposure, kidney function, potassium/magnesium, interacting medicines and conduction/rhythm context are explicitly reviewed.

fields.label: IV amiodarone eligibility reviewed?
options: Prior amiodarone exposure, haemodynamics, QT/interaction context and cardioversion/stroke safeguard reviewed
High risk, prior exposure, QT/interaction/haemodynamic concern, or review incomplete
fields.threshold: Do not use a generic IV amiodarone regimen until prior exposure, haemodynamics, QT/interaction context and its potential cardioversion/stroke implications are explicitly reviewed.

fields.label: Definite AF duration for planned cardioversion
options: 48 hours or longer, or onset not definite
fields.threshold: Do not silently merge guideline thresholds. ESC 2024 does not recommend planned cardioversion after >24 hours without 3 weeks therapeutic anticoagulation or TOE excluding thrombus; ACC 2023 uses AF duration ≥48 hours for that pre-cardioversion safeguard.

fields.label: Pre-cardioversion thromboembolism safeguard
options: At least 3 weeks therapeutic anticoagulation verified
fields.threshold: For non-emergency planned cardioversion, document duration and one guideline-aligned thrombus/anticoagulation plan. Both source sets require post-cardioversion anticoagulation review; this guide does not select, dose or authorize an anticoagulant.

stages.title: Entry & cause review
stages.empty: Confirm rhythm, pre-excitation screen, ventricular-response context, instability and acute trigger.

stages.title: Immediate escalation
stages.empty: No attributable instability or pre-excitation emergency route is selected.

stages.title: Rate / rhythm strategy
stages.empty: Select a source-aligned strategy after entry and safety fields are explicit.

stages.title: Reassess response
stages.empty: Review observed rhythm/rate, BP, perfusion, symptoms, trigger and medication exposure after intervention.

stages.title: Cardioversion & stroke safeguards
stages.empty: Keep anticoagulation/stroke review separate from rate response.

quickReference.summary: Confirm AF, exclude pre-excitation, cardiovert attributable instability, choose one monitored stable rate strategy, and keep acute-trigger plus thromboembolism review separate from rate response.
recognition: Review the ECG rhythm/QRS pattern, BP/perfusion, symptoms, acute heart failure, ischaemia, mental status and whether the tachyarrhythmia is the driver of instability.
Evaluate acute triggers in parallel: sepsis, hypoxaemia, ischaemia, fluid overload/depletion, cardiogenic shock, electrolytes and medication effects.
Reconcile all recent AV-nodal exposure before repeating or adding a rate-control agent.
redFlags: Hypotension, shock, acute altered mental status, ischemic chest discomfort or acute heart failure attributable to the tachyarrhythmia.
Wide-irregular rhythm or pre-excitation concern: avoid beta-blocker, diltiazem/verapamil, digoxin and IV amiodarone.
Decompensated heart failure, critical illness, worsening response, medication-timing overlap, unknown onset before planned cardioversion, or unresolved anticoagulation/TOE safeguard.

steps.text: AHA ACLS: immediate synchronized cardioversion if instability is attributable to AF/flutter with RVR. For confirmed AF on a US-approved biphasic device, initial energy is at least 200 J; sedate whenever feasible without delaying care.
steps.dosingNote: Use the device and local resuscitation protocol; the engine does not configure shocks, pads, waveform or sedation.

steps.text: Choose one route: esmolol 500 mcg/kg IV over 1 min then 50–300 mcg/kg/min, or diltiazem 0.25 mg/kg IV over 2 min then 0.35 mg/kg after 15 min if needed (LVEF >40% route).
steps.dosingNote: Reconcile recent AV-nodal therapy and reassess BP/perfusion before any repeat or additional agent.

steps.text: Digoxin and IV amiodarone are conditional fallback reviews, not automatic co-loading. Planned cardioversion preserves ESC >24-hour and ACC ≥48-hour pre-cardioversion safeguards separately.
steps.dosingNote: No anticoagulant, antiarrhythmic, pump, local-product or cardioversion order is created.

monitoring: Continuous rhythm monitoring with repeated BP/perfusion, symptoms and ECG/rhythm review around acute intervention.
Reassess acute trigger, LV/HF context, kidney function, potassium/magnesium and interacting medication exposure before a fallback agent.
Document the rate/rhythm strategy, observed response, cardioversion duration/safeguard decision when relevant, stroke-prevention review and follow-up plan.

entry.title: Confirm presentation and urgency
entry.scope: Unknown findings remain unconfirmed; assess immediate danger before selecting a treatment phase.

fields.label: Tachyarrhythmia established for this episode?
fields.threshold: Assess whether the rate fits the clinical condition. AHA notes tachyarrhythmia is typically ≥150/min; the number alone does not determine treatment.

fields.label: Current cardiopulmonary compromise?
fields.threshold: Assess hypotension, altered mental status, shock, ischemic chest discomfort or acute heart failure. Current compromise overrides a prior improvement.

fields.label: Current wide-complex morphology?
fields.threshold: Sustained polymorphic VT needs immediate unsynchronized shock, regardless of a reassuring stability selection.

fields.label: Pre-excited AF / accessory-pathway concern?
fields.threshold: Pre-excited AF: avoid adenosine, beta-blockers, diltiazem/verapamil, digoxin and IV amiodarone. Obtain urgent specialist rhythm review.

fields.label: Reversible causes reviewed?
fields.threshold: Review oxygenation, ischemia, electrolytes, medications/toxins and other acute illness in parallel.

fields.label: Recent rhythm-drug exposure?
options: Already given / timing or dose uncertain
fields.threshold: Reconcile actual doses and responses. Do not restart a loading sequence; use response review after treatment.

fields.label: Standard adenosine regimen suitable?
options: Peripheral IV; no asthma/bronchospasm or transplant concern
fields.threshold: Asthma/bronchospasm excludes routine adenosine. Central access or heart transplant can require a much lower dose; obtain expert review.

fields.label: Selected stable wide-complex strategy?
fields.threshold: Choose one expert-monitored strategy. Adenosine is only an option for a stable, regular, monomorphic rhythm; these are not combined loading instructions.

fields.label: Selected infusion safety reviewed?
fields.threshold: Procainamide: exclude prolonged QT and heart failure. Review QT, interactions, BP and delivery for amiodarone; no routine route for pre-excited AF.

fields.label: Observed response?
fields.threshold: Use current rhythm and perfusion above. An earlier conversion does not cancel a recurrence or current instability.

quickReference.summary: Identify the rhythm and its effect on perfusion before selecting a treatment.
recognition: Confirm pulse and ECG mechanism; assess clinical rate appropriateness.
redFlags: Sustained polymorphic VT: immediate unsynchronized shock.
Compromise caused by organized tachyarrhythmia: synchronized cardioversion; do not delay for drugs.
Pre-excited AF excludes routine AV-nodal drugs and IV amiodarone.

steps.text: Stable regular narrow rhythm: vagal maneuvers, then eligible adenosine. Stable regular monomorphic wide rhythm: expert-guided selection of one strategy.
Review current rhythm, perfusion and actual treatment; do not restart loading automatically.

monitoring: ECG, BP, oximetry, rhythm/perfusion response and reversible causes.

entry.scope: Unknown findings remain unconfirmed; assess immediate danger before selecting a treatment phase.

fields.label: Bradycardia episode established?
fields.threshold: Rate is typically <50/min; assess appropriateness for the clinical condition. A low monitor number alone is not the diagnosis.

fields.label: Current cardiopulmonary compromise?
fields.threshold: Assess hypotension, altered mental status, shock, ischemic chest discomfort or acute heart failure. Treat other causes of instability in parallel.

fields.label: High-degree AV block concern?
fields.threshold: High-degree block with instability needs urgent pacing-capable review. Do not delay pacing for repeated drug attempts.

fields.label: Bradycardia with compromise persists after initial support?
fields.threshold: Support airway, provide oxygen/ventilation as needed, attach monitoring and reassess the pulse. This question records the response to support; it must agree with current rhythm and compromise.

fields.label: Atropine suitability reviewed?
fields.threshold: Confirm clinical indication and patient-specific cautions. Suspected toxicologic cause, unusual conduction/transplant context or other concern needs expert assessment; the guide does not establish suitability from dose history.

fields.label: Total atropine already administered in this episode?
fields.threshold: Use actual administration history, including prehospital doses. 0.5 mg is an older regimen; do not infer a repeat dose from an unrecognized cumulative total.

fields.label: Atropine repeat interval and indication verified?
fields.threshold: Reassess current perfusion and count every prior dose. Never exceed a total of 3 mg. This selection is not a timer.

fields.label: Response to atropine already administered?
fields.threshold: A current deterioration overrides previous improvement. Ineffective atropine permits pacing and/or a reviewed infusion; there is no requirement to wait for the maximum cumulative dose.

fields.label: Monitored infusion plan verified by treating team?
options: Agent, access, dilution and pump reviewed
fields.threshold: Confirm patient-specific indication, prior/concurrent vasoactive drugs, ECG/BP monitoring, line, concentration and pump. Dopamine and epinephrine are alternatives, not an automatic combination.

fields.label: Current response since initial treatment?
fields.threshold: Update current rhythm and cardiopulmonary compromise above. A prior improvement label must not override current emergency findings.

Confirm pulse, ECG and current perfusion.

Hypotension, altered mental status, shock, ischemic chest discomfort or acute HF.

1 mg IV, repeat every 3–5 min if needed, maximum total 3 mg. Reconcile actual prior doses.

Confirm electrical and mechanical capture with pacing.

entry.title: Is this an acute asthma exacerbation?
entry.guidance: Establish likely asthma, an alternate/additional cause, or anaphylaxis. Severe and life-threatening findings require emergency escalation even before a review phase is chosen.

source.label: GINA Strategy Report 2026 — acute-care exacerbations (adult branch; Box 9-6, pp. 184–189)

entry.scope: Confirm an acute worsening consistent with asthma; assess dangerous features and anaphylaxis before choosing the treatment phase.

fields.label: Review phase
fields.essential: Select Initial assessment to view source-based rescue actions, or Response / recovery only after initial treatment. Until a phase is selected, routine asthma dosing stays withheld but emergency escalation still appears.

fields.label: Acute presentation
fields.threshold: Entry: establish likely asthma, an alternative/additional cause, or anaphylaxis. Current GINA acute-care assessment specifically considers pneumothorax, inducible laryngeal obstruction, pneumonia, cardiac failure and pulmonary embolism alongside asthma.

fields.label: Highest current presentation severity
fields.threshold: GINA mild: all features, including full sentences, can lie down, room-air SpO₂ ≥94% and PEF/FEV₁ >70%. Moderate: phrases/preferred sitting, increased respiratory rate or accessory use, reduced air entry, room-air SpO₂ ≥92% or PEF/FEV₁ 50–70%. Severe includes inability to speak, drink or lie down; respiratory rate >30/min; quiet/silent chest; PEF/FEV₁ <50%; or room-air SpO₂ <92%. Drowsiness, confusion or cyanosis needs life-threatening assessment now.

fields.label: Room-air SpO₂ category (before oxygen, if safely measured)
fields.threshold: GINA Box 9-6 uses room-air SpO₂ <92% as a severe feature; <90% in adults signals aggressive therapy. For adult severe asthma, the GINA narrative targets oxygen at 93–95%; the all-age flowchart displays 92–95%.

fields.label: Repeated or high-dose SABA already given?
fields.essential: High SABA exposure can cause tachycardia, hypokalemia, arrhythmia, lactic acidosis and hyperventilation; these can mimic worsening asthma.

fields.label: Response after initial treatment
fields.threshold: GINA reviews symptoms, oxygen saturation and lung function after initial bronchodilator treatment and at 1 hour or earlier. A current response does not erase a severe feature or an alternative diagnosis.

fields.label: Persistent hypoxemia after initial treatment?
fields.threshold: This branch considers a single IV magnesium sulfate 2 g infusion over 20 minutes after inadequate initial response with persistent hypoxemia. Other source indications, including very low initial FEV₁, require separate specialist review; magnesium is not routine.

fields.label: Recovery criteria for discharge review
fields.threshold: GINA Box 9-6 discharge review requires mild signs for 1–2 hours after the last salbutamol, room-air SpO₂ ≥92%, PEF/FEV₁ >70% personal best/predicted, and adequate home resources. These support review; they do not authorize discharge.

stages.title: Entry & escalation
stages.empty: Complete asthma entry, severity and oxygenation review. Unknown does not establish a lower-risk route.

stages.title: Initial rescue
stages.empty: Select Initial assessment to view the source-based rescue branch.

stages.title: Reassess response
stages.empty: Review observed response after initial treatment and at 1 hour or earlier.

stages.title: Recovery / disposition
stages.empty: Recovery needs marked improvement and explicit discharge-review criteria.

quickReference.summary: Establish asthma versus anaphylaxis or another cause, escalate severe findings, separate initial rescue from observed response, and do not turn improvement into automatic discharge.
recognition: Assess speech, air entry, work of breathing, respiratory rate, consciousness, room-air oxygenation and PEF/FEV₁ where feasible; start treatment concurrently when danger is apparent.
Ask what treatment has already been given and the response. Repeated SABA can produce a toxicity pattern that resembles treatment failure.
Look in parallel for anaphylaxis, pneumothorax, inducible laryngeal obstruction, pneumonia, cardiac failure and pulmonary embolism.
redFlags: Drowsiness, confusion, cyanosis, quiet/silent chest, exhaustion, poor effort, instability, worsening gas exchange or airway-protection concern.
Room-air SpO₂ <92%, especially <90%; severe symptoms, PEF/FEV₁ <50%, no response or worsening after initial treatment.
Anaphylaxis with asthma: epinephrine first, then immediate bronchodilator therapy through the emergency pathway.

steps.text: GINA Box 9-6: salbutamol 6–10 puffs plus ipratropium 4 puffs by pMDI/spacer, or nebulized salbutamol 5 mg plus ipratropium 0.25 mg; repeat up to 3 treatments 20–30 minutes apart.
steps.dosingNote: Use one ipratropium-containing route and verify the local product/device; a maintenance frequency is not an acute rescue schedule.

steps.text: Adult severe asthma: controlled oxygen target 93–95%. Start typical adult prednisone/prednisolone 50 mg/day early when indicated; the discharge-course range is 40–50 mg/day for 5–7 days.
steps.dosingNote: Life-threatening presentation uses 100% oxygen by non-rebreather while emergency support is arranged; IV steroid depends on oral-route failure and local protocol.

steps.text: Reassess after the initial bronchodilator series and at 1 hour or earlier. Consider IV magnesium 2 g over 20 minutes only after inadequate initial response with persistent hypoxemia.
steps.dosingNote: Marked improvement alone is not discharge. Confirm sustained mild signs, room-air SpO₂, lung function and home resources, then complete controller/action-plan/follow-up review.

monitoring: Closely monitor oxygen saturation; document device/flow where oxygen is used and do not withhold needed oxygen merely to obtain a room-air value.
After high/repeated SABA, review pulse/rhythm, potassium and lactate in context as well as airflow and work of breathing.
For persistent or worsening symptoms, reassess the diagnosis and critical-care need rather than only repeating the prior regimen.

entry.title: Does the presentation suggest anaphylaxis?
entry.scope: Review acute onset, skin/mucosal findings and airway, breathing or circulation compromise. Skin signs may be absent; urgent treatment must not wait for completed criteria.

fields.label: Acute onset in minutes to several hours?
fields.threshold: WAO criteria use an acute onset in minutes to several hours. An uncertain timeline does not make current airway, breathing or circulation findings safe.

fields.label: Typical skin or mucosal findings?
fields.threshold: Typical findings include generalized hives, pruritus/flushing, or swollen lips, tongue or uvula. Skin/mucosal findings may be absent in anaphylaxis.

fields.label: Laryngeal / airway involvement at acute presentation?
options: Present — stridor, voice change, or throat/tongue swelling
fields.threshold: WAO criterion 2 includes acute laryngeal involvement after a known or probable allergen. Any current airway compromise needs emergency assessment without waiting for this presentation-criteria form.

fields.label: Bronchospasm or respiratory compromise at acute presentation?
options: Present — wheeze, dyspnoea, hypoxaemia, or bronchospasm
fields.threshold: Respiratory compromise is a WAO criterion and an RCUK airway/breathing/circulation emergency feature. For isolated lower-respiratory symptoms, complete the visible WAO exception check before criterion 2 is marked met.

fields.label: Circulation compromise at acute presentation?
fields.threshold: WAO includes reduced blood pressure or collapse. Current cardiac arrest starts the resuscitation algorithm; IM absorption is then unreliable. Current ABC is entered separately after treatment begins.

fields.label: Severe gastrointestinal symptoms?
options: Present — severe crampy pain or repetitive vomiting
fields.threshold: WAO criterion 1 includes severe gastrointestinal symptoms with acute skin/mucosal involvement, especially after a non-food allergen.

fields.label: Known or highly probable allergen just before onset?
fields.threshold: WAO criterion 2 uses a known or highly probable allergen with acute laryngeal, respiratory, or circulation compromise. Do not delay rescue while trigger history is incomplete.

fields.label: Only lower-respiratory symptoms after a common inhalant or perceived food inhalation without ingestion?
options: No — not this isolated lower-respiratory exception
Not applicable — laryngeal, circulation, or additional systemic findings
fields.threshold: WAO criterion 2 excludes isolated lower-respiratory symptoms triggered by common inhalant allergens and perceived food “inhalational” reactions without ingestion. If only bronchospasm is entered, unknown does not automatically meet criterion 2; assess this exception while treating any current ABC danger.

fields.label: Review state
options: Before first IM adrenaline dose — confirmed not yet given
fields.essential: Choose a treatment state to keep initial rescue, a timed repeat dose, refractory care and observation separate. Until selected, ABC assessment remains visible and urgent.

fields.label: Acute onset in minutes to several hours?
fields.threshold: WAO criteria use an acute onset in minutes to several hours. An uncertain timeline does not make current airway, breathing or circulation findings safe.

fields.label: Typical skin or mucosal findings?
fields.threshold: Typical findings include generalized hives, pruritus/flushing, or swollen lips, tongue or uvula. Skin/mucosal findings may be absent in anaphylaxis.

fields.label: Laryngeal / airway involvement at acute presentation?
options: Present — stridor, voice change, or throat/tongue swelling
fields.threshold: WAO criterion 2 includes acute laryngeal involvement after a known or probable allergen. Any current airway compromise needs emergency assessment without waiting for this presentation-criteria form.

fields.label: Bronchospasm or respiratory compromise at acute presentation?
options: Present — wheeze, dyspnoea, hypoxaemia, or bronchospasm
fields.threshold: Respiratory compromise is a WAO criterion and an RCUK airway/breathing/circulation emergency feature. For isolated lower-respiratory symptoms, complete the visible WAO exception check before criterion 2 is marked met.

fields.label: Circulation compromise at acute presentation?
fields.threshold: WAO includes reduced blood pressure or collapse. Current cardiac arrest starts the resuscitation algorithm; IM absorption is then unreliable. Current ABC is entered separately after treatment begins.

fields.label: Current laryngeal / airway involvement?
options: Present — stridor, voice change, or throat/tongue swelling
fields.threshold: This is a current-response finding after treatment starts. Any present airway compromise needs emergency assessment immediately; unknown is not an absent airway threat.

fields.label: Current bronchospasm or respiratory compromise?
options: Present — wheeze, dyspnoea, hypoxaemia, or bronchospasm
fields.threshold: This is a current-response finding after treatment starts. Any present breathing compromise needs emergency assessment immediately; unknown is not an absent respiratory threat.

fields.label: Current circulation compromise?
fields.threshold: This is a current-response finding after treatment starts. Cardiac arrest starts the resuscitation algorithm; unknown is not an absent circulation threat.

fields.label: Severe gastrointestinal symptoms?
options: Present — severe crampy pain or repetitive vomiting
fields.threshold: WAO criterion 1 includes severe gastrointestinal symptoms with acute skin/mucosal involvement, especially after a non-food allergen.

fields.label: Known or highly probable allergen just before onset?
fields.threshold: WAO criterion 2 uses a known or highly probable allergen with acute laryngeal, respiratory, or circulation compromise. Do not delay rescue while trigger history is incomplete.

fields.label: Only lower-respiratory symptoms after a common inhalant or perceived food inhalation without ingestion?
options: No — not this isolated lower-respiratory exception
Not applicable — laryngeal, circulation, or additional systemic findings
fields.threshold: WAO criterion 2 excludes isolated lower-respiratory symptoms triggered by common inhalant allergens and perceived food “inhalational” reactions without ingestion. If only bronchospasm is entered, unknown does not automatically meet criterion 2; assess this exception while treating any current ABC danger.

fields.label: Previous IM dose(s) verified as the adult IM-adrenaline route?
options: Confirmed appropriate adult IM adrenaline dose(s)
Given, but product, route, dose, or timing is uncertain
fields.threshold: Adult RCUK IM rescue uses 500 micrograms (0.5 mL) from a 1 mg/mL preparation in the anterolateral thigh. Do not treat a product with an unknown concentration or an IV preparation as a verified IM dose.

fields.label: Time since the last IM adrenaline dose?
fields.threshold: RCUK repeats IM adrenaline after 5 minutes if airway, breathing, or circulation problems persist. This is a categorical timing check, not a dose calculator.

fields.label: Current beta-blocker exposure?
fields.threshold: Beta-blocker exposure can affect refractory-treatment review; it does not replace IM adrenaline, IV fluid, or critical-care escalation.

fields.label: Symptoms fully resolved after treatment?
fields.threshold: Observation timing starts only after resolution. A normal current ABC finding alone does not establish complete symptom resolution.

fields.label: IM-adrenaline treatment course?
fields.threshold: NICE NG258 uses the number of IM doses in observation risk stratification. The special supervised-allergy-challenge exception is outside this engine.

fields.label: Previous biphasic reaction?
fields.threshold: NICE NG258 assigns at least 6 hours of observation after resolution when there is a history of biphasic reaction.

fields.label: Severe asthma or severe respiratory compromise in this reaction?
fields.threshold: NICE NG258 assigns at least 12 hours after resolution for severe asthma or anaphylaxis involving severe respiratory compromise.

fields.label: Continuing allergen absorption possible?
fields.threshold: NICE NG258 assigns at least 12 hours after resolution when continuing absorption is possible.

fields.label: Out-of-hours, unable to respond to deterioration, or difficult emergency access?
fields.threshold: NICE NG258 assigns at least 12 hours after resolution for these discharge-access risks.

fields.label: All 2-hour fast-track conditions confirmed?
options: Yes — prompt single-dose response, two in-date trained injectors, and supervision
fields.threshold: All required: good response within 5–10 minutes to one IM dose given within 30 minutes of symptom onset; all symptoms resolved; two in-date auto-injectors with knowledge of when/how to use them; adequate adult supervision if needed. A qualified clinician may consider discharge after observation, not automatically.

stages.title: Entry & ABC
stages.empty: Complete the visible entry and ABC assessment.

stages.title: Immediate rescue
stages.empty: No current rescue branch is established from the entered findings.

stages.title: Timed reassessment
stages.empty: Record response and actual administration times.

stages.title: Observation & follow-up
stages.empty: Observation begins only after complete symptom resolution.

quickReference.summary: Treat airway, breathing, or circulation compromise immediately; separate initial IM rescue, a 5-minute repeat, refractory specialist escalation, and post-resolution observation.
recognition: WAO criteria are met by acute skin/mucosal plus systemic involvement, or acute laryngeal/respiratory/circulation involvement after a known or probable allergen; skin may be absent.
When clinical assessment suspects adult anaphylaxis, RCUK uses IM adrenaline 500 micrograms from confirmed 1 mg/mL in the anterolateral thigh, with a 5-minute repeat for persistent ABC problems.
redFlags: Airway/laryngeal involvement, respiratory compromise, hypotension/collapse, altered consciousness, or cardiac arrest.
Persistent respiratory or circulation symptoms after two appropriate IM doses: refractory anaphylaxis needs immediate critical-care support.
Any proposed IV adrenaline bolus, product concentration ambiguity, unverified prior dose, persistent/recurrent symptoms, or high-risk observation feature.

steps.text: Assess acute onset, skin/mucosal features, trigger, and ABC. Do not wait for a completed diagnostic entry to call for help and treat ABC compromise.

Initial adult IM dose is 500 micrograms (0.5 mL from 1 mg/mL) in the anterolateral thigh. If one dose has been given and ABC features persist, repeat after 5 minutes; reconcile actual timing and product.

Persistent respiratory/circulation symptoms after two appropriate IM doses need critical-care, monitored infusion-level care under local protocol. After complete resolution, NICE NG258 observation risk categories guide clinician review.

monitoring: Pulse oximetry, non-invasive BP, ECG, ABC trajectory, and exact adrenaline administrations should be monitored/recorded as soon as possible without delaying rescue.

For suspected adult anaphylaxis, NICE NG258: sample tryptase as soon as possible after emergency treatment starts and again ideally at 1–2 hours, no later than 4 hours from onset; specialist follow-up may need baseline tryptase.
